intent: Frame one person's or account's picture in a fixed-size circle and hold the load status its image and fallback share.
typical_uses: The picture of a person or account beside their name
One member of a stacked group of participants

dont_use_when.situation: A picture or icon with no person or account behind it

instead.target: a plain img element or an icon
instead.note: Avatar exists for the image-or-fallback switch of an identity picture; a product thumbnail or a decorative glyph needs none of it.

dont_use_when.situation: A placeholder while the record the avatar belongs to is itself still loading

mounted_in.container: any layout in the consuming application
mounted_in.note: A single avatar sits beside a name or inside any row or header of the application; AvatarGroup is needed only to overlap several of them.

invariants.text: The root holds one image load status (idle, loading, loaded, error) that AvatarImage writes and AvatarFallback reads; it stays idle while no AvatarImage is mounted and returns to idle when the AvatarImage unmounts.
The load status reaches no data attribute on the root or its parts; it is readable only through AvatarImage's `onLoadingStatusChange` and through the state the `render` and `style` functions receive.

`size` sets the circle's width and height, and avatar.module.css reads the root's size class back in the parts: the badge's diameter steps with every size and the fallback's text takes the smaller meta text size at `sm`; the parts take no size of their own.
The root rounds itself but sets no `overflow: hidden`; the image and the fallback each round themselves, which is what lets AvatarBadge sit on the circle's edge without being cut off.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass the picture's `src` or `alt` to Avatar itself
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put them on an AvatarImage inside the Avatar - the root is a span frame and renders no image of its own

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the avatar's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the avatar's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (imageLoadingStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through avatar.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A picture with initials shown until it loads
A large avatar with a status badge

bad.title: The image source passed to the root
bad.why: Avatar forwards to a span and declares no `src` or `alt`; nothing loads and the root renders an empty circle. The picture is an AvatarImage child, with an AvatarFallback beside it for while it loads or when it fails.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, AvatarRootState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the avatar's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: AvatarRootState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the avatar's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (imageLoadingStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through avatar.module.css, not through this.
